extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors submitting probability research to the Annals of Probability
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors about what kinds of papers the Annals of Probability accepts — scope, emphasis, and that authoritative reviews/surveys are welcome. Focused on research in modern probability theory and its mathematical and scientific relations/applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of publishable work
rubrics_metrics.description: The Annals of Probability publishes research papers in modern probability theory, its relations to other areas of mathematics, and its applications in the physical and biological sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers should fall within modern probability theory or clearly connect probability to other mathematical areas or to applications in physical/biological sciences; submissions outside this stated scope are not appropriate for the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on importance, interest, and originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasis is on importance, interest, and originality – formal novelty and correctness are not sufficient for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal expects work to demonstrate substantial significance and broad interest in addition to technical correctness or formal novelty; authors should make the case for why results matter and are of interest to the probability community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and timeliness of review papers/surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: The Annals will also publish authoritative review papers and surveys of areas in vigorous development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey/review submissions should be authoritative, synthesize and clarify rapidly developing areas, and be of clear value to readers; the journal solicits such pieces when they address topics undergoing active advancement.
